column4: Knots with Signature 4 and Determinant 4k+1: An Answer to a Question of Shinohara — Alper Ferudun (Mercury Software GmbH), version1.0, 2026-10-02, existing unrefereed AI-assisted preprint DOI10.5281/zenodo.23111900; actual concept DOI10.5281/zenodo.23111899. Full affirmative answer to the unrestricted original question: for every integer n>1 congruent1 mod4, a tame knot in S3 has determinant n and signature4. Theorem1.1 and Lemmas3.1–3.2 were inspected in the actual archived nine-page PDF: integral Seifert matrices, CRT/Dirichlet/reciprocity for nonsquares, a divisor branch, and a six-dimensional block for remaining squares; genus at most2 outside the remaining-square case and at most3 there, with no universal genus2 claim. Classical Seifert realization, Dirichlet, reciprocity, CRT and Sylvester inputs are explicit. All three actual archived payloads match recorded sizes/checksums; every one of46 ZIP entries/41files passes CRC. Source-author programs and their broader computational, classification, lattice-sketch, knot-table and minimal-crossing claims were not replayed or certified. The original Ohtsuki page and essential Ferudun proof were independently read; attempted1971 Shinohara body access failed, so no claim of reading it or exhaustive historical priority is made. New exact bounded arithmetic/matrix diagnostics pass normal/-O/-OO, supplementing the universal written proof. This independent review is AI-only, unrefereed and not a new project theorem or new DOI upload. PR: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1294
